tips: C1 · mitigate (v): make less serious. "This patch mitigates the risk of data loss."
C1 · ambiguous (adj): open to more than one meaning. "The requirement is ambiguous about empty input."
C1 · discrepancy (n): a difference that shouldn't exist. "There's a discrepancy between the logs and the database."
C1 · streamline (v): make simpler and more efficient. "Let's streamline the deploy process."
C1 · deprecate (v): mark as outdated, to be removed later. "We deprecated the v1 endpoint."
C1 · redundant (adj): not needed, because something else already does it. "This null check is redundant."
C1 · robust (adj): strong; handles errors and edge cases well. "Make the parser more robust to bad input."
C1 · consolidate (v): combine into one stronger whole. "Consolidate the three config files into one."
C1 · feasible (adj): possible and practical. "Is it feasible to migrate this week?"
C1 · trade-off (n): what you give up to gain something else. "Caching is a trade-off between speed and freshness."
C1 · bottleneck (n): the slowest part, which limits the whole. "The database query is the bottleneck."
C1 · intermittent (adj): happening on and off. "The test fails intermittently on CI."
C1 · pinpoint (v): find the exact cause or place. "Help me pinpoint where the memory leak starts."
C1 · tentative (adj): not final; may change. "Here's a tentative plan for the refactor."
C1 · comprehensive (adj): complete; covers everything. "Write comprehensive tests for the parser."
C1 · concise (adj): short but complete. "Give me a concise summary of the changes."
C1 · elaborate on (v): explain in more detail. "Could you elaborate on the second option?"
C1 · leverage (v): use something to full advantage. "Leverage the existing cache instead of adding Redis."
C1 · overhaul (n): a complete, major update. "The auth module needs an overhaul."
C1 · legacy (adj): old but still in use. "Don't change the legacy API yet."
C1 · workaround (n): a temporary way around a problem. "Is there a workaround until the fix ships?"
C1 · constraint (n): a limit you must work within. "Constraint: no new dependencies."
C1 · implication (n): a likely effect or result. "What are the implications for existing users?"
C1 · rationale (n): the reasons behind a decision. "Explain the rationale for this design."
C1 · backward compatible (adj): still works with older versions. "Keep the API backward compatible with v2 clients."
C1 · inadvertently (adv): by accident. "This change inadvertently broke the login page."
C1 · exhaustive (adj): checking every possibility. "That list of edge cases isn't exhaustive."
C1 · granular (adj): detailed, in small parts. "We need more granular permissions."
C1 · overlook (v): fail to notice. "I overlooked the time zone issue."
C1 · cumbersome (adj): slow and awkward to use. "The current setup process is cumbersome."
C1 · viable (adj): able to work successfully. "Is SQLite a viable option here?"
C1 · adhere to (v): follow a rule or standard. "Adhere to the existing naming conventions."
C1 · refine (v): improve with small changes. "Let's refine the error messages."
C1 · outline (v): describe the main points. "Outline the steps before writing any code."
C1 · address (v): deal with a problem. "This PR addresses the race condition."
C1 · assess (v): judge the size or quality of something. "Assess the impact of this change."
C1 · obsolete (adj): no longer used or needed. "Remove the obsolete migration scripts."
C1 · explicit (adj): stated clearly, not implied. "Make the return type explicit."
C1 · underlying (adj): the real cause, under the surface. "Fix the underlying issue, not the symptom."
C1 · susceptible to (adj): easily affected by. "This query is susceptible to SQL injection."
C1 · alleviate (v): make a problem less bad. "Pagination will alleviate the load on the API."
C1 · expedite (v): make something happen faster. "Can we expedite the review?"
C1 · meticulous (adj): very careful about details. "Be meticulous with the migration script."
C1 · coherent (adj): logical and clear. "Make the docs more coherent."
C1 · arbitrary (adj): chosen without a clear reason. "Why is the timeout an arbitrary 37 seconds?"
C1 · inherent (adj): a basic, built-in part of something. "Some latency is inherent in this design."
C1 · contingency plan (n): a plan for when things go wrong. "What's our contingency plan if the deploy fails?"
C1 · caveat (n): a warning or limit to keep in mind. "One caveat: this only works on macOS."
C1 · nuance (n): a small but important difference. "There's a nuance between 'should' and 'must'."
C1 · iterate on (v): improve by repeating steps. "Let's iterate on the design."
C1 · accommodate (v): make room for; support. "The schema should accommodate future fields."
C1 · circumvent (v): find a way around a rule or limit. "Don't circumvent the rate limiter."
C1 · substantial (adj): large or important. "This is a substantial change, so split it into smaller PRs."
C1 · scrutinize (v): examine very carefully. "Scrutinize the diff before merging."
C1 · corroborate (v): confirm with more evidence. "The logs corroborate the user's report."
C1 · infer (v): work out from evidence. "What can we infer from this stack trace?"
C1 · prone to (adj): likely to suffer from. "This function is prone to off-by-one errors."
C1 · counterintuitive (adj): the opposite of what you'd expect. "It's counterintuitive, but the smaller cache is faster."
C1 · in hindsight (phrase): looking back now. "In hindsight, we should have added tests first."
C1 · as opposed to (phrase): instead of; in contrast with. "Use a queue, as opposed to polling every second."
